messages:
morgan: Ran helm template as part of the GitOps CI for the inference-gpu chart and got a weird rendering when .Values.gpus.allowedZones is an empty array. CI shows a stray `-` in the YAML which makes kustomize/apply fail. Example snippet from our template:
```
{{- range .Values.gpus.allowedZones }}
- name: {{ . }}
{{- end }}
```
When allowedZones is `[]` or not set we end up with a dash and then an empty line. Anybody seen this?

alex: yup, Helm's `range` will still render block markers if you have newlines around it. Usually wrap with an `if` or use a helper to coalesce to a list. e.g. `{{- if .Values.gpus.allowedZones }}{{- range ... }}...{{- end}}{{- end}}` or `{{- $zones := default (list) .Values.gpus.allowedZones }}` and `range $zones`.

sam: also check values.schema.json — if the schema doesn't set a default empty array, users can pass `null` which behaves differently. Lint shows no error because `helm template` is permissive, but kustomize/YAML parsers are strict about sequence entries without content.

jen: quick workaround is to make the helper produce nothing when empty. in `_helpers.tpl` we have a `listify` helper in other charts: `{{- define "common.list" }}{{- $v := default (list) . }}{{- if $v }}{{- range $v }}...{{- end}}{{- end}}{{- end }}`. We can add a `coalesceList` helper and use that across gpu-related templates.

morgan: deploy-bot posted the CI failure details here: FAILED step `gitops/helm-template` — rendered manifest contained an empty sequence entry at inference-gpu/templates/node-affinity.yaml:12. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 :exclamation:

helm-lint-bot: Suggest add `"default": []` to values.schema.json for `gpus.allowedZones` and add a unit test to the helm-template job that runs `helm template` with `--values=tests/values-empty.yaml` to catch regressions. Also recommend `yq`-based post-render validation to catch stray `-` tokens.

alex: agree with schema default + helper. Small gotcha: `default (list)` only works in Helm 3 templating if you import the `list` function correctly — but that should be fine. Also watch trimming whitespace with `{{-` vs `{{` — that often changes whether a dash sits on its own line.

sam: I'm seeing another related case: when we `include` a helper that returns nothing, the surrounding indentation can still leave `- ` on the line. We should add tests that run `helm template` and then `kubeval`/`yamllint` to ensure syntactic validity.

morgan: OK I'll open a small PR that: 1) adds `coalesceList` helper in `_helpers.tpl`, 2) updates gpu templates to use it, 3) sets `default: []` in values.schema.json for allowedZones, and 4) adds a CI case `tests/values-empty.yaml`. Assigning to @alex for review.

jen: :thumbsup: thanks — if you want I can paste a minimal helper snippet:  ```{{- define "helpers.coalesceList" -}} {{- $v := default (list) . -}} {{- if $v -}} {{- $v -}} {{- end -}} {{- end -}}```  wrap usage as `{{- range include "helpers.coalesceList" .Values.gpus.allowedZones }}` (might need tweaks).

alex: small nit — `include` returns string, so better to do `{{- $zones := default (list) .Values.gpus.allowedZones }}{{- range $zones }}` inside the template rather than include for ranges.

morgan: noted. I'll use the `$zones` approach. Pushing draft PR in ~30m. Thanks all.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline created: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipelines/67890 (job: helm-template-empty-values). It will run the new test after PR lands.

sam: awesome — once merged we should backport to the 1.2.x branch used by Dedicated clusters to avoid surprises during rollouts.

morgan: will add backport label. Closing thread for now, will post PR link when ready. :white_check_mark:
